title: Enabling Multiple Tensor-wise Operator Fusion for Transformer Models on Spatial Accelerators
problem: In transformer models, data reuse within individual operators is insufficient, prompting the need for more aggressive multiple tensor-wise operator fusion. Conventional fusion techniques fail to achieve this due to limited dataflow options and inability to handle long fusion chains.
motivation: Effective multi-operator fusion can significantly improve computational efficiency and resource utilization of transformer workloads on spatial accelerators for both edge and cloud deployments.
method: Dataflow Adaptive Tiling (DAT) treats multiple chained operations as a single unit and systematically explores different ways to route data between them. For each data-routing option, it checks if the intermediate results fit in the spatial accelerator's on-chip buffer (the fast memory attached to the processor), then selects the best-performing configuration. Unlike earlier approaches, this works with operations connected in any pattern and any chain length.
key_novelty: DAT enables fusion of multiple operations regardless of how they're connected, by automatically finding the best data-routing pattern that fits within the accelerator's on-chip memory.
contributions: Identification and formalization of three key challenges in multi-tensor operator fusion for transformers
Novel Dataflow Adaptive Tiling (DAT) framework for inter-operator dataflow design enabling arbitrary operator connections and fusion chains
Exploration framework for rapid dataflow search on spatial accelerators constrained by on-chip buffer capacity
Experimental validation achieving 2.24× speedup and 35.5% energy savings on edge accelerators, 1.74× speedup and 15.5% energy savings on cloud accelerators compared to FLAT
